note: First hardware run of the VREF case, against the regulator device-PM support of zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr#119026 (branch nxp-drivers-restore-after-power-loss, build 72cc1ec0f084). All six layers on the two MCXN boards that have a vref node wired up. Images were converted to Intel hex with arm-none-eabi-objcopy, flashed over `dapeng remote control flash` and captured over the forwarded serial stream.

frdm_mcxn947/mcxn947/cpu0.note: The board overlay asks for NXP_VREF_MODE_HIGH_POWER, and the trim variant resolves to TRIM2V1 as expected for this SoC. Baseline reads CSR 0x00010838 -- the three devicetree bits plus HI_PWR_LV and BUF21EN from the mode -- and the output reads stable within the driver's startup delay. The device layer proves both restore branches: after a clobber, TURN_ON puts the untrimmed device back at the bottom of the range (0x0, 1000000 uV) and, once a consumer has set a voltage, restores that trim instead (0x6, 1600000 uV). Deep Sleep is transparent. Deep Power Down fails the two checks the case documents as expected failures, and the disable/enable recovery afterwards passes, so the block itself comes back healthy.

frdm_mcxn236.note: Identical to frdm_mcxn947 layer for layer, register value for register value.

dpd.mcxn: regulator-initial-mode restored after the transition -- CSR comes back 0x00000038: the devicetree bits are restored by TURN_ON, HI_PWR_LV and BUF21EN are not, because the mode is applied only by regulator_common_init() at boot.

output stable after the transition for a held reference -- VREFST reads 0 although the reference count still shows the consumer's reference. The trim survives in retained SRAM and the voltage still reads 1600000 uV, so what is missing is the re-enable, not the setting.

findings.summary: With runtime device PM the vref block is never given its devicetree configuration, because the TURN_ON that carries it never runs.
findings.detail: Baseline in the runtime and system layers reads CSR 0x00010800: the mode bits that regulator_common_init() writes are there, the three devicetree bits (ICOMPEN, CHOPEN, REGEN) are not. The device boots in OFF rather than SUSPENDED because its domain -- &core_domain, a power-domain-soc-state-change node -- is itself runtime enabled and is suspended right after its own init, so pm_device_is_powered() is already false when regulator_nxp_vref_init() runs and pm_device_driver_init() skips TURN_ON. A later pm_device_runtime_get() does not repair it: that domain forwards TURN_ON only on the system state changes it lists, so the device goes from OFF to ACTIVE on a bare RESUME and CSR still reads 0x80010807 after the cycle. A consumer can enable the output and set a voltage in this state, so nothing reports an error -- the reference just runs without the current compensation, chopping and internal regulator the devicetree asked for. Reproduced on both boards.

findings.summary: The runtime layer captured zero bytes on both boards: a NULL dereference in the power-domain driver at PRE_KERNEL_1.
findings.detail: Same root cause as the PORT run; see results/20260916-port-dapeng.json for the analysis and the verified one-line guard.
